review_notes.assessment: stop() precedes reset(): prior completed peaks can still be cached, pipeline streaming is stopped before peak mutation, and the previous QThread is joined. Reset clears peaks and position/index before either early return; a cache hit copies the cached peaks back synchronously. m_currentFile remaining unchanged on an early return cannot trigger a stale cache write because m_playbin is null.

The timer and builder QObject retain owner-thread affinity; there is no moveToThread or run override. Error-path stop therefore joins the separate default QThread event loop, not itself. update() holds its own bus and popped-message references across pipeline teardown and releases them afterward, matching the existing EOS path. No access to m_playbin follows stop() in update(). Incomplete peaks are not written to cache.

review_notes.assessment: New-screen observers are registered synchronously while QScreen is valid. Deferred recovery reads the current screen list and does not dereference removed-screen signal arguments. Connections and zero-delay lambdas have this as lifetime context. Native normal-state restoration is deferred and rechecks state before applying/clearing the normal geometry cache.

Malformed settings are length/conversion checked. Geometry policy uses individual logical work areas rather than a bounding union, preserves usable partial/negative/spanning placement, ignores invalid screens and bounds fallback size. Minimized/maximized/fullscreen notifications adjust only cached normal geometry; hidden normal windows are moved/resized without being shown. Explicit maximize/fullscreen exits restore and clear cache before subsequent user moves.

Qt5-specific QDesktopWidget calls remain guarded and now select availableGeometry(this); added QScreen/connect/timer APIs are compatible with the project's Qt5.15 baseline by inspection. Frameless windows now participate in state-change recovery rather than returning early. Windows test linkage names the production taskbar sources and platform libraries. No native Windows/Qt5 build verdict is inferred from this inspection.
